_note: Delaware Coast Live. Every record here describes a camera someone else operates. Delaware Beach Finds does not host, record, re-stream, or archive any of this video. A feed is only embedded when permissionStatus is 'platform-embed' or 'approved'; every other state renders as a link-out card to the operator's own page. Never add an embedUrl obtained by bypassing a restriction, and never imply an operator endorses Delaware Beach Finds.

_permissionStatus.platform-embed: Public video on a platform whose ordinary embed mechanism is enabled by the operator (verified). Safe to embed with attribution.
_permissionStatus.approved: Operator has given Delaware Beach Finds explicit written permission. Record the permission in permissionNotes.
_permissionStatus.public-upstream: Official public-agency feed consumable through normal browser playback without circumvention.
_permissionStatus.external-only: Renders as a card linking to the operator's page. Used when there is no supported embed, or when embedding would require permission we do not have.
_permissionStatus.pending: Outreach in progress. Renders as external-only until resolved.

feeds.title: Cape Henlopen Osprey Cam
feeds.owner: Friends of Cape Henlopen State Park
feeds.permissionNotes: Public YouTube stream published by Friends of Cape Henlopen State Park. Embedding verified enabled via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-08-19. Nothing is proxied, recorded or re-hosted.
feeds.attribution: Camera courtesy of Friends of Cape Henlopen State Park
feeds.description: A nesting platform on the point at Cape Henlopen, rebuilt in 2023 and re-fitted in 2025. Ospreys return to the Delaware coast in spring, and the platform is usually busiest from first light to mid-morning.

feeds.title: Cape Henlopen Nature Center Feeder
feeds.location: Seaside Nature Center, Cape Henlopen State Park
feeds.owner: Friends of Cape Henlopen State Park
feeds.permissionNotes: Public YouTube stream published by Friends of Cape Henlopen State Park. Embedding verified enabled via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-08-19.
feeds.attribution: Camera courtesy of Friends of Cape Henlopen State Park
feeds.description: A feeder outside the Seaside Nature Center. Cardinals, chickadees and red-bellied woodpeckers are routine; turkey and deer turn up often enough to be worth waiting for.

feeds.title: DelDOT Coastal Traffic Cameras
feeds.location: Route 1 and the Delaware coastal corridor
feeds.permissionNotes: DelDOT publishes its cameras through an interactive map application with no documented public feed endpoint. We link to the official DelDOT map rather than guess at internal URLs or route the feed through a third party.
feeds.attribution: Cameras operated by the Delaware Department of Transportation
feeds.description: Before you commit to the drive: DelDOT's own camera map covers Route 1 and the coastal corridor. Worth a look on a Friday afternoon in season, and after any beach-day thunderstorm.

feeds.title: Bethany Beach Boardwalk Cameras
feeds.permissionNotes: The town serves its cameras through a third-party vendor page (48half.com) embedded on its own site. Re-embedding a vendor page we have no relationship with is not something we will assume permission for. Ask the town first.
feeds.attribution: Cameras operated by the Town of Bethany Beach
feeds.description: The town's own cameras look down the boardwalk and over the bandstand — the quickest way to see what the south end of the Delaware coast is doing right now.

feeds.title: Ocean City Boardwalk & Inlet Cameras
feeds.location: Ocean City boardwalk, inlet and beach
feeds.permissionNotes: Ocean City's cameras run on IPCamLive under aliases belonging to OC Tourism. The platform has an embed mechanism, but the cameras are theirs — we ask before we embed rather than assume a public alias is an invitation.
feeds.attribution: Cameras operated by the Town of Ocean City, Maryland
feeds.description: Fenwick runs straight into Ocean City, and plenty of Delaware weekends end up on that boardwalk. The town's cameras cover the inlet, the beach and the boards.
